Flameshot - Powerful yet simple to use screenshot software.

summary.one_liner: Flameshot is an open-source screenshot application for Linux, Windows, and macOS with a built-in annotation editor, configurable hotkeys, and CLI capture commands.
summary.what_it_does: Flameshot runs as a background process with an optional system tray icon and captures screenshots through CLI commands such as `flameshot gui`, `flameshot full`, and `flameshot screen`. Captures can be delayed, saved to a custom path, copied to the clipboard, or printed as PNG bytes. The GUI capture mode offers in-app editing with tools for pencil, line, arrow, rectangle, circle, marker, text, and pixelate, plus undo/redo and a screenshot history. Captures can be copied, saved, opened in another app, or uploaded to Imgur. The README also documents a DBus interface, a config file (flameshot.ini), CLI config options, and setup steps for triggering captures from Print Screen on KDE Plasma, GNOME, XFCE 4, and Fluxbox.
use_cases: Take screenshots with annotations on Linux desktops
Capture a delayed screenshot of hover tooltips
Bind Print Screen to a custom capture tool
Script full-screen or per-monitor captures from the command line
Blur or pixelate sensitive areas before sharing an image
Upload a screenshot to Imgur quickly
notable: Annotation editor with shapes, text, marker, and pixelate tools, plus on-capture color picker
Scriptable CLI with options for delay, output path, clipboard copy, and per-screen capture
Step-by-step Print Screen hotkey setup for KDE Plasma, GNOME, XFCE 4, and Fluxbox
Packaged through many Linux distributions, MacPorts, Homebrew, and Scoop
Windows build includes flameshot-cli.exe for console output
caveats: Wayland support is described as experimental on Gnome and Plasma, and wlroots compositors need separate setup
Minimal X11 window managers may need extra configuration because no portal backend provides the Screenshot interface
Building from source requires Qt 6.2.4 or newer, GCC 11 or newer, and CMake 3.22 or newer, and source installs have no uninstaller
On macOS the app may be blocked by Gatekeeper and needs manual approval
